_comment: The clip vocabulary the game needs, written for a motion diffusion model.
Prompts are short, physical and present-tense; Kimodo responds to verbs and body
parts, not to cinematic adjectives. 'loopable' is a hint, not a guarantee - the
trimmer in retarget-soma.mjs is what actually makes a cycle loop.
frames are at 30 fps. Locomotion clips are deliberately LONGER than one gait
cycle so a whole cycle can be cut out of the steady middle and the ragged
calib-right-arm is not a game clip. It is the handedness falsifier: SOMA's rest
skeleton is mirrored relative to glTF (see scripts/animation/soma30.mjs), and the
only honest way to prove the correction is to ask for a named side and check which
of OUR bones ends up raised.

prompts.text: a person raises their right arm straight up above their head and holds it there, left arm hanging at their side

a soldier stands at full height with both knees locked straight and his spine vertical, shoulders level, chin up looking straight ahead, both hands holding a rifle in front of his chest, he does not crouch or bend, only a small breathing sway, loopable
prompts.note: REJECTED, both seeds (2026-09-19); the game keeps the AUTHORED idle from clips.ts. Measured from the skinned surface in the game, a helmeted figure on this rig reaches 1.858 m at rest. Seed 1001 ('stands still at ease') gave 1.633 m; seed 1201 ('stands upright and tall') 1.704 m offline; seed 1202 ('both knees locked straight ... does not crouch or bend') 1.706 m offline. The loss is not the lean - 5.9 deg at seed 1202 - it is the cervical chain: the Neck->Head segment measures 0.058 m of its 0.140 m rest length, a 65 deg bow, on every seed. The model will not hold a head up in a standing idle and two seeds is the cap. The brief's fallback is a CMU BVH; the project's own third route - procedural clips authored in code, already licensed and already the library's floor (docs/LICENCES-ANIMATION.md) - is better here, because CMU has no standing idle at all and the authored one stands at 1.838 m with the weapon-carry layer giving it both hands. Left in the library with ship:false so the rejection stays reproducible and measurable.

prompts.text: a soldier walks forward slowly and casually at an unhurried stroll, short relaxed steps, arms swinging gently, loopable
prompts.note: second seed. The first (1002, 'steady relaxed pace') measured 2.14 m/s at the planted foot - a jog, not a walk, and the blend tree would have played it at half timeScale for a 1.1 m/s character.

prompts.text: a soldier jogs forward at a steady pace holding a rifle at the ready, elbows bent, even strides, loopable
a soldier sprints forward flat out at top speed, long fast strides, tall through the chest with the head up, arms driving straight forward and back close to the sides, elbows in, loopable
prompts.note: third prompt (2026-09-19). Seed 1104's 'body low and forward' gave 53.2 deg of left-arm abduction - arms out sideways like a scarecrow - and 1.660 m to the helmet. 'body low' was doing the damage, so the prompt now asks for the arm PATH (forward and back, elbows in) instead of a body attitude.

prompts.text: a soldier holds a half-kneeling combat crouch with his back straight and chest up, knees bent, rifle shouldered, steady
prompts.note: second seed. The first (1005) put the pelvis at 0.288 m - sitting on the heels, head at 0.89 m. A combat crouch keeps the torso upright, so the prompt now says so instead of saying 'low'.

prompts.text: a soldier advances in a combat crouch, back straight and chest up, knees bent, taking short steady steps, rifle shouldered, loopable
prompts.note: second seed. The first (1006, 'torso low') produced a duck-walk: pelvis 0.52 m with the torso near horizontal. Photographed at captures/anim/crouchwalk-side.png before the re-roll.

prompts.text: a soldier stands upright with his legs straight and his back vertical, head level, aiming a rifle straight ahead with both hands at shoulder height, elbows tucked in close to his ribs, holding steady, loopable
prompts.note: second prompt (2026-09-19). Seed 1007 measured 1.719 m to the helmet and 15.9 deg of torso lean - the model crouched into the shot. Legs, back and head are now named separately from the weapon, because naming only the weapon lets the model choose the stance.

prompts.text: a soldier walks forward slowly while aiming a rifle straight ahead with both hands, upper body steady, loopable
a person crouches and then jumps straight up off both feet, tucking the knees at the top
a person lands from a drop, absorbing the impact by bending both knees deeply, then straightens back up
a person standing still pivots ninety degrees to their left on the spot, feet stepping around
a person standing still pivots ninety degrees to their right on the spot, feet stepping around
a soldier firing a rifle absorbs the recoil, the shoulders and head jolting back sharply and then resettling
a soldier lowers a rifle slightly, brings his right hand down to his belt and up to the weapon, then raises the rifle again
a person is struck hard in the chest and staggers backward, torso recoiling, arms flinching
a person is shot, buckles at the knees and collapses forward onto the ground, ending face down and motionless
